descriptor: Operating company · reported in CNY · quoted in HKD

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Net income here is profit attributable to shareholders. Since the FY2023 baijiu (Jin Sha) acquisition, consolidated profit including the 44.81% minority stake has diverged: FY2025 profit including NCI was RMB 3,174m versus RMB 3,371m attributable, i.e. minority holders absorbed a ~RMB 197m loss that period while shareholders' line still rose.

charts.title: Shareholders' Equity vs Total Liabilities
charts.annotation: Shareholders' equity above is attributable to owners only. Non-controlling interests (minority stake in the Jin Sha baijiu business, acquired FY2023 for RMB 9,709m cash) sit alongside it in total equity and ran RMB 3.6-3.9bn FY2023-H1 2026 -- not shown as a column because the CSV does not carry it, but a real claim on the consolidated balance sheet.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage. The line above is equity attributable to shareholders only.

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: total equity also carries non-controlling interests (NCI) -- the 44.81% minority stake in the Jin Sha baijiu business bought for RMB 9,709m cash in FY2023 -- running RMB 3.6-3.9bn FY2023-H1 2026. It is a real slice of consolidated net assets that this chart's equity line excludes, and goodwill from the same acquisition sits inside total assets.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions
  • NCI balance relative to shareholders' equity -- a growing minority claim dilutes how much of the baijiu business's assets actually belong to CRB shareholders

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: FY2023's dip (RMB 1,629m, well below net income) is largely the RMB 9,709m cash paid to acquire the majority stake in the Jin Sha baijiu business, a one-off investing outflow rather than a decline in the core beer business's cash generation. The gap between net income and owner FCF in other years is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income outside of acquisition years
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF
  • Future M&A cash outflows funded by debt rather than organic FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: net income shown here is profit attributable to shareholders, after deducting the non-controlling interest (NCI) share. CRB acquired a majority stake in the Jin Sha baijiu business in FY2023 for RMB 9,709m cash, consolidating 100% of it while a 44.81% minority stake (NCI, RMB 3.6-3.9bn on the balance sheet FY2023-H1 2026) keeps a claim on its results. The two profit lines can move in opposite directions: FY2025 profit attributable to shareholders was RMB 3,371m while consolidated profit including NCI was only RMB 3,174m, because minority holders absorbed roughly a RMB 197m loss that year even as the shareholders' line held up -- baijiu integration risk showing up as a wedge between the two measures, not in revenue.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)
  • Widening gap between profit attributable to shareholders and profit including NCI -- a sign the baijiu integration is absorbing more of the swing than the headline NPAT shows

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China Resources Beer (Holdings) Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
